name: Allam-Fetvedt cycle (oxy-combustion supercritical CO2 power)
applications: natural gas power with inherent capture

source.note: IEAGHG review of current and emerging CO2 capture technologies, TCCS-10, June 2019, Task 1 TRL tables

principle: Natural gas burns in oxygen diluted with hot recycled CO2. The high-pressure CO2 and water mixture drives a turbine, is cooled in a recuperator, and the water is condensed out. Most CO2 is recompressed and recycled; the excess is near-pure and goes straight to a pipeline.

suppliers.name: NET Power (cycle developer), Toshiba (combustor and turbine)

reference_plants.name: Project Permian (NET Power), west Texas
reference_plants.capacity: initial phase now targets 80 MW, using Siemens A35 gas turbines with Entropy post-combustion capture rather than an Allam-Fetvedt cycle plant
reference_plants.status: FID expected second half 2026, commercial operation targeted early 2029 (as of March 2026)

source.note: NET Power Q4 and full-year 2025 results, 9 March 2026

advantages: Capture is inherent to the cycle; no separate capture plant
limitations: New turbine and combustor technology; first commercial plants not yet operating as of the source

gaps.item: whether any utility-scale Allam-Fetvedt cycle plant is still planned
gaps.reason: NET Power's March 2026 update describes its first commercial project as gas turbines with post-combustion capture; it does not say when or whether an Allam-cycle plant follows. RESOLVED NEGATIVE 2026-10-28: no utility-scale Allam-cycle plant is under construction or firmly planned. NET Power is running demonstration-plant testing campaigns through 2026 (FY2025 10-K, Mar 2024), and in January 2026 withdrew the interconnection request for its proposed Midcontinent clean power hub (Energy Intelligence); the MIT CCS project database lists the 295 MW scale-up as cancelled/inactive. The first commercial NET Power projects have pivoted to conventional gas turbines.
